title: No database – data lives in JSON files
context: The app is a prototype for exploring the triage workflow; persistence and multi-user editing are out of scope.
decision: Store requests, triage output, requirements and decisions in /data/*.json and read them at build time. Revisit once editing from the UI is needed.

title: triage.json is the source of truth for themes
context: Many incoming requests describe the same need in different words, and raw requests should stay exactly as the client sent them.
decision: Themes, their requestIds and scores live in triage.json. requirements.json only holds the requirement doc per theme. Requests not in any theme are listed as unclustered.

title: Next.js App Router with Server Components
context: Pages are read-only views over static data.
decision: Render pages as Server Components and prerender them statically. Only the nav, the board (card selection) and the requests table (sorting) are Client Components.

title: Fictional tour-operator demo data
context: Real client requests cannot be published in a public repository.
decision: Use 22 made-up requests from 6 fictional tour operators, marked as fictional in the JSON files and in a banner on every page.

title: Board columns follow the score ranking
context: A status workflow (New → Done) says nothing about what to build first.
decision: Rank themes by score: #1 goes to Now, #2–4 to Next, the rest and unclustered requests to Inbox. Columns are derived, not stored.
